independence: Did not author the source changes, regression tests, issue requests or generation evidence. Independent date subreview delegated to /root/sssom_adversarial_review/date_probe. No code/data edits, remote mutations, provider calls, merges or branch deletion performed.
scope: Exact committed generator follow-up for issues 684-686, plus preservation of earlier B5/K/G repairs. Native science/identity rules inspected; API and output failure boundaries checked. Review is not a scientific approval or claim of merge.

issue_outcomes.evidence: Curated local namespace controls B1 alias even when primary slug differs. Actual sodium nitrate stock YAML retains its exact ingredient primary and receives an ingredient subject alias. Every shared old/new row payload is unchanged.

Mixed-case primary is preserved exactly while lowercase B1 alias uses the same namespace. Independent encoded/mixed-case matrix passes both native B1 and B5; avoiding alias synthesis by casefold alone would not satisfy B1.

Calendar-valid ASCII history dates supply header date; invalid history warns and cannot outrank valid entries. Empty dates remain explicit native Rule F diagnostics if another row supplies header date. Entirely dateless and malformed emitted-date failures report all tested offenders and preserve destination bytes.

commands_and_results.result: 23 date regression tests passed. Combined with independent61 identity/synonym tests,84 focused tests passed.

Native YAML→main→TSV→native F/G probe, all-dateless destination preservation,17 malformed emitted-date cases, calendar/Unicode/type/order controls passed. See date result for exact invocation and observations.

test_coverage_assessment: Actual sodium nitrate stock and synthetic reverse namespace controls distinguish curated primary namespace from ontology-parent inference.

Independent270-case matrix crosses both local namespaces, matching/mixed/different slugs, encoded/non-ASCII filenames, five ontology parent families and three mapping grades;30 cases differ from prior generator and now retain one local namespace.
Native B1 and B5 run on every matrix case and the changed actual record, so passing a builder-only assertion cannot hide a mismatch with current MIM invariant semantics.

Real-source comparison reads2,680 mapped YAML files with identical empty enrichment inputs. Only sodium nitrate stock changes; old/new shared row payloads are byte-for-value identical. No primary identifier, predicate, synonym or curation date is silently rewritten.

Native F/G integration confirms both dateless synthetic subjects remain visible to Rule F; an all-dateless CLI run names all four subjects and leaves sentinel output unchanged.17 malformed emitted dates all appear in one refusal before writing.

Date tests cover ASCII/calendar parsing, invalid-history coexistence with a valid date, fullwidth/Arabic-Indic forms, implicit YAML date/datetime values, leap centuries and years0001/9999; no wall-clock fallback was introduced.

Public CLI options and helper call signatures remain unchanged. Empty-date behavior is deliberately restored to the documented native Rule F boundary; no native validator or exemption baseline was changed.

An additional mixed dated/dateless fixture passed default builder validation without --no-validate and independent SSSOM JsonSchema/PrefixMapCompleteness/StrictCurieFormat validation; native F still names exactly both dateless subjects and G passes.
limitations: Complete native regeneration, full CLAW suite, mypy and broader CI checks are owned by the parent task and are not claimed as independently rerun here.
Whole-source row comparison uses empty enrichment/residual dictionaries to isolate this delta; it is not fresh ontology validation or a replacement for actual generator replay.
Scientific identity decisions and historical WITHHOLD mappings remain outside this mechanical review. No namespace was selected beyond retaining the existing curated local primary namespace.
Date extraction intentionally validates the date prefix; timestamp time-of-day/timezone validity is outside this helper contract.

Rule B5 still groups namespace conflicts by subject plus casefolded slug. This review verifies the builder no longer introduces cross-namespace aliases in the tested paths; it does not claim a new validator-wide scientific identity policy.
